issue.title: Status of testing Providers that were prepared on November 27, 2025
issue.body:
### Body

I have a kind request for all the contributors to the latest provider distributions release.
Could you please help us to test the RC versions of the providers?

The guidelines on how to test providers can be found in

[Verify providers by contributors](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/dev/README_RELEASE_PROVIDERS.md#verify-the-release-candidate-by-contributors)

Let us know in the comments, whether the issue is addressed.

These are providers that require testing as there were some substantial changes introduced:

comments.body: Checked mine. All good. also checked a few of those .whl files >= 2.11.0 is all good.
Checked mine as well.Good to go from my side. #58349

I think the provider versions and the links are not correct, right? Normally they should point to a `*rc1` version. E.g. it should be [discord: 3.11.0rc1](https://pypi.org/project/apache-airflow-providers-discord/3.11.0rc1/)

I have successfully tested all my changes with Airflow==3.1.3:

#56911 ✅

I installed the pre-release provider packages and ran a test DAG. Asynchronous notifications for Discord have been successfully sent.

@jscheffl I have tested my changes to edge3 and git providers and they look good. 

However -1 on the celery provider. I am seeing the following error when I run `airflow celery -h` after installing celery 3.14.0rc1 with breeze . 

Steps to reproduce:
```
breeze start-airflow --executor CeleryExecutor --use-airflow-version 3.1.3 --airflow-extras celery -d -e
# In tmux
pip install apache-airflow-providers-celery==3.14.0rc1
airflow celery -h  
```


cc: @ephraimbuddy

update: 
looks like this works when I also upgrade common compat package along with it 
`pip install apache-airflow-providers-common-compat==1.10.0rc1`
my changes in celery work after this upgrade but upgrade to celery 3.14.0 would require upgrade of common-compat to 1.10.0

@dheerajturaga thanks for testing and letting us know! Yeah this is really a problem with celery but also affecting aws and microsoft-azure. Reason is that with moving Exceptions to common compat the minim requirement to common-compat was not increased to be at least 1.10. The provider reference still refers to minimum common-compat 1.8 (which probably you had installed).

I need to pull these three providers out of the release and we can consider running a rc2 later.
Checked mine. Good to go from my side. #57369
I have verified that #58568 for the Microsoft azure provider is working as expected

Thank you everyone. Providers are released.

I invite everyone to help improve providers for the next release, a list of open issues can be found [here](https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Aarea%3Aproviders).
